question: Can a TD-error-seeking exploration rule that detects and caps persistently high-TD-error transitions reach the sparse-reward goal faster than the plain TD-error-seeking rule in a small stochastic-reward gridworld?
method: Tabular Q-learning with error-seeking action selection on a simulated gridworld (sparse goal, noisy costly cells). Learning runs over agent seeds; main score is mean environment steps to first goal on held-out evaluation seeds. The improved stuck threshold and cap quantile are chosen jointly by leave-one-training-env-out CV on training seeds only; the candidate set includes 'no cap' (= baseline rule).

dataset.name: Simulated stochastic-reward gridworld (generated in code)
dataset.source_url: none: generated in code, no download

metric_name: mean environment steps to first goal on held-out evaluation seeds (lower is better; capped at the step budget)
baseline: Tabular Q-learning; actions chosen by argmax of running mean |TD error| per state-action pair (stand-in for SEE's error-seeking objective), eps=0.05.
improved: Same agent, but each state-action pair keeps a TD-error history; pairs whose |TD error| stays high without decaying are flagged stuck (threshold chosen by CV from 0.25/0.5/1.0) and their exploration value is capped at a visited-value quantile (0, 0.25 or 0.5) or left uncapped, chosen by leave-one-training-env-out CV.
notes: Simulated toy environment; tabular Q-learning, not SAC with neural networks, so this is only a stand-in for SEE. Only the improved variant's stuck threshold and cap were tuned, by CV on TRAIN_ENV; the baseline and the test seeds were not used for selection. The candidate set includes the no-cap rule, so the selected setting is no worse than the baseline on training seeds; test results can still differ. Steps are censored at the step budget. Only three agent seeds and three training envs make the CV noisy; no significance test.
